title: Buying a car: five criteria, nonlinear and linear models

source.citation: Rezaei, J. (2019). BWM: Best Worst Method. Lecture slides, slides 21-25: the car-buying example solved with the nonlinear model of Rezaei (2015), Omega 53, 49-57, and the linear model of Rezaei (2016), Omega 64, 126-130.
source.location: Slides 21-25 (vectors, Model (2) with interval weights, consistency ratio, Model (5))
source.note: Published by the method's author on the method's website. Both Omega papers are paywalled (doi:10.1016/j.omega.2014.11.009, doi:10.1016/j.omega.2015.12.001); see docs/methods/bwm.md.

nonlinearIntervals.printedIn: Slide 23, optimal interval of each weight

deviations.note: Slide 25 swaps the comfort and safety weights of the linear model; the unique LP optimum is comfort 0.1231, safety 0.1538.
Slide 25 swaps the comfort and safety weights of the linear model; the unique LP optimum is comfort 0.1231, safety 0.1538.
Slide 25 prints 0.061; the linear programme gives xi_L* = 4/65 = 0.06154, which rounds to 0.062. Truncated on the slide.

notes: The nonlinear model (Rezaei 2015) min xi s.t. |w_B / w_j - a_Bj| <= xi, |w_j / w_W - a_jW| <= xi has optimum xi* = 1 here, but not a unique weight vector: each weight ranges over the interval printed on slide 23. The slide reports the interval centres, as recommended in Rezaei (2016). A golden test must check xi*, the intervals and the centres, never a single solver-dependent optimum.
Consistency ratio = xi* / CI with CI = 4.47 for a_BW = 8 (Rezaei 2015, Table 5). CI solves xi^2 - (1 + 2 a_BW) xi + (a_BW^2 - a_BW) = 0.

The linear model (Rezaei 2016) has a unique solution. Slide 25 prints comfort 0.154 and safety 0.123; the linear programme gives comfort 0.1231 and safety 0.1538, which is also the only order consistent with a_B,comfort = 4 > a_B,safety = 3. The slide swapped the two values (deviations).
xi_L* = 0.061 is reported by the author as the consistency measure of the linear model; it is not divided by CI.
